subject.title: [Feature]: When building a work system with OpenClaw as the core, WebUI should remain accessible after the Gateway crashes.

question: Should OpenClaw core own a crash-survivor same-port Control UI fallback after the Gateway process exits, and if so what supervisor or rescue-sidecar security model should be supported?
rationale: This cannot be resolved as a narrow bug fix because it adds core availability architecture, public config surface, and security-boundary behavior beyond the current single-process Gateway model.

options.title: Sponsor core rescue design
options.body: Keep the issue open and require a maintainer-owned design for a supervised rescue/static sidecar with auth, origin, TLS, config, and upgrade proof before implementation.

options.title: Document external supervision only
options.body: Decide that systemd/launchd/container orchestrators or a reverse proxy own crash pages, then close or re-scope this issue to documentation gaps.

options.title: Explore plugin or API seam
options.body: Keep the issue open only to identify a missing plugin or supervisor API rather than adding one-off Gateway fallback behavior.

recommendation.title: Sponsor core rescue design
recommendation.body: Keep the issue open and require a maintainer-owned design for a supervised rescue/static sidecar with auth, origin, TLS, config, and upgrade proof before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter has the strongest sampled history across Gateway server/runtime and Control UI ownership surfaces touched by the architecture decision.
